Guidance for Claude Code working inside the `magic_devtools` repo. Path-scoped rules live in `.claude/rules/`.

**Version:** 1.1.0 · **Dart:** >=3.13.0 · **Flutter:** >=3.47.0 · **Requires:** `magic`, `magic_socket`, `tapir`, `crumbs`, `wind_kit`, `material_ui`

## What this package is for, and why it is a package at all

`magic_devtools` is the seam between `magic` and the dev tooling: the adapters that wire `tapir` and `crumbs` into a running Magic app, plus a dev-only component preview catalog.

It exists so that `magic` core keeps zero dependency on tapir and crumbs: a production app depends on magic without dragging an E2E driver and a runtime inspector into its resolution graph. Every consumer adds this package as a regular dependency imported only under `!kReleaseMode` (a dev_dependency would trip `depend_on_referenced_packages`), so release builds tree-shake it.

Every install call is guarded by `!kReleaseMode` at the call site, in the consumer's `main.dart`, and never inside a method here: debug and profile builds carry the tools, so a perf measurement runs on a profile build. Moving the guard inward defeats the release tree-shake and pulls both tools into the production bundle, the one failure this package's whole shape is arranged to prevent.

tapir and crumbs depend on neither magic nor each other (tapir reads wind only through `wind_kit_diagnostics_contracts`), so anything that joins them is assembled here: tapir reads crumbs through function pointers this package assigns (`pendingHttpCountReader`, `recentLogsReader`, `recentExceptionsReader` from `MagicCrumbsIntegration`, the perf readers from `MagicPerfIntegration`), and three of the fourteen enrichers read `CrumbsStore` directly.

## Commands

| Task | Command |
|:-----|:--------|
| Test | `flutter test --coverage` |
| Analyze | `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` |
| Format | `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` (run it before pushing: a branch that never ran the formatter fails in CI and nowhere earlier) |
| Docs gate | `python3 tool/check-docs.py` |
| Pre-publish | `dart pub publish --dry-run` |

Local sibling development goes through the gitignored `pubspec_overrides.yaml` with absolute paths (`.worktreeinclude` explains why). The committed `pubspec.yaml` stays on hosted caret constraints so a fork outside this workspace resolves on its own.

## Architecture

```
lib/
├── magic_devtools.dart   # Umbrella barrel: MagicDevtools.installPre / installPost
├── tapir.dart            # MagicTapirIntegration: 14 snapshot enrichers, MagicRouter navigate adapter
├── crumbs.dart           # MagicCrumbsIntegration: 6 Magic watchers, MagicHttpFacadeAdapter
├── preview.dart          # Component preview catalog barrel
└── src/                  # Private implementation; perf lives here too (MagicPerfIntegration)
doc/                      # User docs, published by the docs site: getting-started/, basics/, guides/
skills/magic-devtools/    # Agent skill, installed with `npx skills add anilcancakir/magic_devtools`
example/                  # Runnable app showing the install order and the release guards
tool/check-docs.py        # Offline docs gate, run by docs-link-check.yml
```

The four barrels are the API: reach for a narrow barrel only when wiring one tool without the other, or when a host wants a non-standard watcher set. Dependency direction is one way: `magic_devtools` depends on the crumbs and tapir contracts, and neither of those ever depends on magic.

## The two-phase install is a contract

`installPre` runs before `Magic.init()`; `installPost` runs after. Neither half can move.

- **Pre** boots `TapirPlugin` and `CrumbsPlugin` and registers crumbs' opt-in `ExceptionWatcher` and `DumpWatcher`. It has to be early so the snapshot pipeline and the exception watcher are live while Magic boots: they capture boot-time errors and the first route resolve, the window a later install misses.
- **Post** wires Magic's runtime in. Its watchers, HTTP adapter and enrichers resolve dependencies through the IoC container (`Magic.find` / `Magic.bound`), so `Magic.init()` must have completed.

Decide which half new wiring belongs to by asking what it resolves: anything that touches the container is post; anything that must observe Magic booting, or registers with a subsystem that locks its table on first read (the router does), is pre. Every install is idempotent, so a second call in the same isolate is safe; keep it that way.

## Post-Change Checklist

After any source code change, sync before committing. A change is not done while one of these is stale:

1. **`CHANGELOG.md`**: an entry under `[Unreleased]`
2. **`README.md`, `llms.txt` and the `doc/` pages**: update when features, API or usage change, and run `python3 tool/check-docs.py`
3. **`skills/magic-devtools/SKILL.md`**: update when the API, a rule or a gotcha changes; its `version:` moves with the release and `publish.yml` compares it with the tag
4. **`CLAUDE.md`**: update the architecture tree when files move

## Development Flow (TDD)

Every feature, fix or refactor goes through red, green, refactor: write a failing test that fails for the right reason, write the minimum code to pass it, then clean up with the tests green. No production code without a failing test first; `flutter analyze` clean, `dart format` with zero diff and `flutter test` green before pushing.

## Testing

- Each integration has a `resetForTesting()`; pair it with the other packages' resets in `tearDown`.
- `MagicTapirIntegration.resetForTesting()` removes each enricher it added, one by one, so an enricher added to the install list without a matching removal leaks into the next test.
- Tests mirror `lib/src/` in `test/` and import through a barrel (`magic_devtools.dart`, `tapir.dart`, `crumbs.dart` or `preview.dart`).

## Key Gotchas

| Mistake | Fix |
|:--------|:----|
| An enricher that keeps the `Element` between calls | An enricher is `String? Function(Element, RefRegistry)`, synchronous and stateless; never retain the `Element` |
| Two enrichers emitting the same snapshot key | tapir does not deduplicate keys and both lines reach the output; keep every key distinct |
| Moving a `!kReleaseMode` guard inside this package | The guard stays at the consumer's call site, or release builds carry both tools |
| Adding a dependency that lets magic core reach tapir or crumbs | Keep the direction `magic_devtools` to contracts; never the other way |
| Putting container work in `installPre` | Anything that resolves `Magic.find` or `Magic.bound` belongs in `installPost` |
| Relative paths in `pubspec_overrides.yaml` | Use absolute ones; the file is never committed |

## Style

English only, types everywhere, docblocks on every public class and contract saying why rather than restating the signature. Multi-line collections with trailing commas, 120-character lines, no linter suppressions. No em dash or en dash anywhere, including commits and PR bodies: use a comma, colon, semicolon, period or parentheses.

## Branching and Release

One long-lived `master`. Task branches (`feat/*`, `fix/*`, `docs/*`, `chore/*`) are cut from master and merged back with a merge commit, never a squash.

1. Open a `release:` PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml`, `skills/magic-devtools/SKILL.md` and the `Version:` line above, and promotes `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. After it merges, tag the merge commit with the bare version (`git tag 1.0.1 <merge-sha> && git push origin 1.0.1`, no `v`). `publish.yml` runs from the tag; the pub.dev Admin tab holds repository `anilcancakir/magic_devtools`, tag pattern `{{version}}` and push events only.
3. A failed `Validate` is fixed forward: delete the tag, fix it on a PR and tag the new merge commit, because a re-run builds the same commit.

## CI

- `ci.yml`: push or PR, then `flutter pub get`, analyze, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`, `flutter test --coverage`, codecov upload
- `changelog.yml`: a PR that changes `lib/`, `test/` or `pubspec.yaml` must also change `CHANGELOG.md`; Dependabot, `release:` PRs and the `skip-changelog` label are exempt
- `docs-link-check.yml`: every PR runs `python3 tool/check-docs.py` and an offline lychee pass; Mondays an external-link pass
- `publish.yml`: tag on master, then version stamps (tag, pubspec, skill), analyze, format, test, dry-run, pana 160/160, changelog section, OIDC publish, GitHub Release, registry sync
